<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 5 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Fields</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">5.3</span> Tensor Fields and notation</h1></header>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>A <span class="dg-term dg-term-red">(smooth) <span class="math inline">\( (r,s) \)</span>-tensor field</span> is a <span class="math inline">\( C^\infty(\mathcal{M}) \)</span>-multilinear map  <span class="math display">\[
            T : \underbrace{\Gamma T^* \mathcal{M} \times \dots \times \Gamma T^* \mathcal{M}}_{r\text{-terms}} \times
            \underbrace{\Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \dots \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M}}_{s\text{-terms}}
            \overset{\scriptstyle \begin{array}{c}
                \sim \\[-10pt] ... \\[-6pt] \sim
            \end{array}}{\longrightarrow} C^\infty(\mathcal{M}).
        \]</span>  In particular, a <span class="math inline">\((0,1)\)</span>-tensor field is a covector field, i.e. an element of <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma T^* \mathcal{M}\)</span>, and a <span class="math inline">\((1,0)\)</span>-tensor field is a vector field, i.e. an element of <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma T \mathcal{M}\)</span> (since the dual of <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma T^* \mathcal{M}\)</span> is <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma T \mathcal{M}\)</span>).</p></li>
<li><p>So far, given a chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\)</span> around <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, we have expanded vectors and covectors at that point in the chart-induced bases of <span class="math inline">\(T_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(T^*_p\mathcal{M}\)</span> which, in the compact notation of Subsections <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/tangent-space.html#notation_TpM" data-kind="subsection" data-label="notation_TpM">4.1.2</a> and <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/cotangent-space.html#notation_TstarpM" data-kind="subsection" data-label="notation_TstarpM">4.2.2</a>, read  <span class="math display">\[
            \begin{aligned}
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        v_{\gamma, p} = x^i_p \, (\partial x_i)_p
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
                \quad ; \quad
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        (df)_p = \mathtt{x}_i^p \, (dx^i)_p,
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
            \end{aligned}
        \]</span>  with <span class="math inline">\(x^i_p = \dot{\gamma}^i_{\mathcal{U}}(\lambda_0)\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\((\partial x_i)_p = \left( \partial / \partial \mathscr{X}^i \right)_p\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{x}_i^p = (df)_p\big((\partial x_i)_p\big)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\((dx^i)_p = (d\mathscr{X}^i)_p\)</span>, and where the Einstein summation convention is implied. Both the components and the basis elements refer to the single point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>At the level of fields, each of these expressions splits into two parts, both of which are promoted from the single point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> to the whole chart domain <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span>:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><strong>Basis fields.</strong> Dropping the point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, as done in Section <a class="dg-xref" href="vector-fields.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Vector_Fields">5.1</a>, the basis elements become smooth sections over <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span>, the chart-induced basis vector and covector fields:  <span class="math display">\[
                    \begin{aligned}
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} : \mathcal{U} &amp;\longrightarrow T\mathcal{U} \\
                                p &amp;\longmapsto \left( \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \right)_p
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                        \quad ; \quad
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                d\mathscr{X}^i : \mathcal{U} &amp;\longrightarrow T^*\mathcal{U} \\
                                p                            &amp;\longmapsto (d\mathscr{X}^i)_p.
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                    \end{aligned}
                \]</span>  On the overlap <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\)</span> with a second chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\)</span>, they transform as  <span class="math display">\[
                    \begin{aligned}
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} = \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \, \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j}
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                        \quad ; \quad
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                d\mathscr{X}^i = \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \, d\mathscr{Y}^j,
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                    \end{aligned}
                \]</span>  where the entries of the Jacobian are now functions rather than numbers:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
                    \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} : \mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
                    p &amp;\longmapsto \left( \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \right)_p = \partial_j \left[ \mathscr{X}^i \circ \mathscr{Y}^{-1} \right] \big( \mathscr{Y}(p) \big),
                \end{align*}</span>  i.e. <span class="math inline">\(\left( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \right)^i_{j} \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V})\)</span>, and correspondingly for <span class="math inline">\(\partial \mathscr{Y}^j / \partial \mathscr{X}^i = \left( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{V}\mathcal{U}} \right)^j_{i}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Component functions.</strong> The components, real numbers at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, become smooth functions on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span>, obtained by letting each field act on the basis of the other kind:  <span class="math display">\[
                    \begin{aligned}
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                x^i \coloneqq \left. \mathcal{X} \right|_\mathcal{U} \left\lfloor \mathscr{X}^i \right\rceil \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                        \quad ; \quad
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                \mathtt{x}_i \coloneqq \left. df \right|_\mathcal{U} \left\lceil \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \right\rfloor \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U}),
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                    \end{aligned}
                \]</span>  so that, at each point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}(p) = v_{\gamma, p}\)</span>, they return the components above, <span class="math inline">\(x^i(p) = x^i_p\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{x}_i(p) = \mathtt{x}_i^p\)</span>. Denoting by <span class="math inline">\(y^j\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{y}_j\)</span> the component functions w.r.t. <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\)</span>, they transform on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\)</span> as  <span class="math display">\[
                    \begin{aligned}
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                x^i = \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \, y^j
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                        \quad ; \quad
                        &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                            \begin{aligned}
                                \mathtt{x}_i = \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i} \, \mathtt{y}_j.
                            \end{aligned}
                        \end{array}
                    \end{aligned}
                \]</span></p></li>
</ol></li>
<li><p>Putting both parts together, vector and covector fields are expanded over <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span> as  <span class="math display">\[
            \begin{aligned}
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        \left. \mathcal{X} \right|_\mathcal{U} = \underbrace{x^i}_{\in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})} \odot_\Gamma \underbrace{\frac{\partial}{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}}_{\in \Gamma T\mathcal{U}}
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
                \quad ; \quad
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        \left. df \right|_\mathcal{U} = \underbrace{\mathtt{x}_i}_{\in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})} \odot^*_\Gamma \underbrace{d\mathscr{X}^i}_{\in \Gamma T^*\mathcal{U}},
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
            \end{aligned}
        \]</span>  and, extending the compact notation to fields by dropping the point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> from the basis elements and the s-multiplication symbols,  <span class="math display">\[
            \begin{aligned}
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        \left. \mathcal{X} \right|_\mathcal{U} = x^i \, \partial x_i
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
                \quad ; \quad
                &amp;\begin{array}{c}
                    \begin{aligned}
                        \left. df \right|_\mathcal{U} = \mathtt{x}_i \, dx^i.
                    \end{aligned}
                \end{array}
            \end{aligned}
        \]</span>  In the same way, an <span class="math inline">\((r,s)\)</span>-tensor field is expanded over <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span> as  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \left. T \right|_\mathcal{U} &amp;= T^{i_1 \dots i_r}_{j_1 \dots j_s} \;
            \partial x_{i_1} \otimes \dots \otimes \partial x_{i_r} \otimes dx^{j_1} \otimes \dots \otimes dx^{j_s}, \\
            T^{i_1 \dots i_r}_{j_1 \dots j_s} &amp;\coloneqq T\big( dx^{i_1}, \dots, dx^{i_r}, \partial x_{j_1}, \dots, \partial x_{j_s} \big) \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U}),
        \end{align*}</span>  whose component functions transform with one Jacobian factor per index, as those of <span class="math inline">\(x^i\)</span> (upper) and <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{x}_i\)</span> (lower) above.</p></li>
<li><p>With this notation the letter “<span class="math inline">\(x\)</span>” appears in several fonts, and its meaning depends on the context: <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}^i\)</span> are the coordinate functions of the chart, <span class="math inline">\(x^i_p\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{x}_i^p\)</span> are real numbers at a point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(x^i\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{x}_i\)</span> are functions on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\((\partial x_i)_p\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\((dx^i)_p\)</span> are basis elements at the point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, while <span class="math inline">\(\partial x_i\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(dx^i\)</span> are the corresponding basis fields over <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span>. Care must be taken to avoid misinterpretation.</p></li>
</ul>
